fullPassage: Some people view old age as inevitably depressing. They assume that the older you get, the greater the deterioration in quality of life. Of course it is true that the longer you live, the more opportunity you have of experiencing negative as well as positive events. And certain illnesses, aches, pains, and disabilities do become more likely with increasing age, as do losses of family, friends, and social support. Therefore, some sadness is to be expected. Nonetheless, depression is absolutely not an inevitable consequence of old age. Most symptoms of depression in the elderly are identical to those in people of all ages. However, the elderly are more likely to focus on the physical and to talk about their aches and pains rather than their feelings of despair. Furthermore, elderly people commonly express regret and remorse about past events in their lives.

questions.passage: Some people view old age as inevitably depressing. They assume that the older you get, the greater the deterioration in quality of life. Of course it is true that the longer you live, the more opportunity you have of experiencing (A)[negative / positive] as well as positive events. And certain illnesses, aches, pains, and disabilities do become more likely with increasing age, as do losses of family, friends, and social support. Therefore, some sadness is to be expected. Nonetheless, depression is absolutely not an (B)[inevitable / avoidable] consequence of old age. Most symptoms of depression in the elderly are (C)[different / identical] to those in people of all ages. However, the elderly are more likely to focus on the physical and to talk about their aches and pains rather than their feelings of despair. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) negative(부정적인), (B) inevitable(불가피한), (C) identical(동일한) — 원문 일치
det.analysis:
✅ ① negative — inevitable — identical: 원문 그대로
❌ ② positive — inevitable — different: positive는 negative의 반의어 (글의 요지와 반대)
❌ ③ negative — avoidable — identical: avoidable은 inevitable의 반의어 (우울증이 피할 수 있는 것이 되어버림)
❌ ④ negative — inevitable — different: different는 identical의 반의어 (노인과 전 연령의 증상이 '다르다'는 오류)
det.tip: negative↔positive, inevitable↔avoidable, identical↔different

det.korean: ④ different(다른)는 원문 identical(동일한)의 반의어 — 노인의 우울증 증상이 전 연령과 '동일하다'는 맥락에서 '다르다'는 표현은 불일치

✅ ② negative: 원문 일치 (부정적 경험)
✅ ③ inevitable: 원문 일치 (피할 수 없는 결과가 아님)

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 <u>view</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) view = 바라보다/관찰하다(시각적 행위), (B) view = ~로 여기다/간주하다(인식/판단)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 바라보다 — (B) 여기다: (A)는 풍경을 '눈으로 바라보는' 시각 행위, (B)는 노년을 '우울한 것으로 간주하는' 인식/판단
❌ ② (A) 여기다 — (B) 바라보다: (A)의 vast landscape는 '간주'가 아닌 '시각' 대상
❌ ③ 둘 다 바라보다: (B)의 'view A as B' 구문은 간주/여기다 의미
❌ ④ 둘 다 여기다: (A)의 경관을 '여기다'는 어색함
det.tip: view의 두 의미: ① 바라보다(look at) — (A) 풍경 관찰 / ② ~로 여기다(regard as) — (B) view A as B 구문

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "a feeling of deep guilt and sorrow for having done something wrong"

det.korean: remorse(자책/뼈저린 후회) — 잘못된 행동에 대한 깊은 죄책감과 슬픔.
det.analysis:
❌ ① despair: 절망/희망 상실, 죄책감 요소가 없음
❌ ② sadness: 단순 슬픔, 잘못에 대한 죄책감과 다름
✅ ③ remorse: 정의 일치 — 잘못된 행동에 대한 깊은 죄책감과 자책
❌ ④ regret: 후회(약한 아쉬움), remorse보다 강도가 약하고 죄책감 요소가 적음
det.tip: remorse = deep guilt + sorrow for wrongdoing(자책). regret(아쉬움)보다 강도 강함.

questions.passage: And certain illnesses, aches, pains, and disabilities do become more likely with __________ (increase) age, as do losses of family, friends, and social support.

disabilities do become more likely with __________ (increase) age.

det.korean: increase(동사원형) → increasing(현재분사/형용사): 전치사 with 뒤에서 명사를 수식하는 현재분사 형용사 역할.
det.analysis: with + 현재분사 → increasing (나이가 '증가함에 따라'). 'with increasing age = 나이가 들수록'이라는 숙어 표현.
det.tip: with increasing age = 나이가 들수록. increase(증가하다, 동사) → increasing(증가하는, 현재분사 형용사)

다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

the greater the __________ (deteriorate) in quality of life.

det.korean: deteriorate(동사원형) → deterioration(명사): 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문에서 the greater the ___ 뒤에는 명사가 온다.
det.analysis: the 비교급, the 비교급 구문 → the greater the [명사] → deterioration (명사화). '나이가 들수록 삶의 질 악화가 더 심해진다'.
det.tip: deteriorate(악화되다, 동사) → deterioration(악화, 명사). the greater the 뒤에 명사 필수.

det.analysis:

❌ ② seek medical treatment for their conditions: 의학적 치료 추구, 신체 집중의 표현 방식 불일치
✅ ③ focus on the physical and to talk about their aches and pains: 원문 일치 — 노인은 감정(절망)보다 신체 증상에 집중
❌ ④ avoid discussing their emotional struggles: 감정 회피, 원문은 '신체에 집중'이지 '감정 회피'가 아님
